children: The Rs 22,569-crore initial public offering (IPO) of the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) closed with investors bidding for 5.71 times the shares on offer, setting the stage for the exchange’s market debut on September 24.

Demand strengthened through the three-day issue after a relatively subdued opening, with qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) emerging as the strongest segment. The institutional portion was subscribed 12.68 times, while the non-institutional investor (NII) quota received bids for 6.55 times the shares reserved for it.
Retail participation was comparatively measured but still crossed the full subscription mark, with the category subscribed 1.39 times. The employee portion was subscribed 2.40 times.

The issue, priced in the Rs 1,700-1,785 range, is the second-largest IPO in India’s history and the biggest public issue so far in 2026. At the upper end of the price band, NSE’s implied market capitalisation stands at around Rs 4.41 lakh crore.

With the subscription window now closed, attention shifts to the allotment process. The basis of allotment is expected to be finalised on September 22, following which shares allotted to successful applicants are scheduled to be credited to their demat accounts on September 23.
NSE shares are scheduled to begin trading on both the BSE and NSE on September 24.
The strong institutional response was the key driver of the overall subscription, with QIB demand accounting for a substantial portion of the bids received during the issue.

Kotak Capital, JM Financial, Morgan Stanley India, Citigroup, HSBC Securities, JPMorgan India, SBI Capital, Anand Rathi Advisors, Avendus Capital, Axis Capital, DAM Capital, Equirus Capital, HDFC Bank, ICICI Securities, IDBI Capital, IIFL Capital, Motilal Oswal, Nuvama Wealth, Pantomath Capital and 360 ONE WAM are the book-running lead managers to the issue.
The listing will mark a significant development for India’s capital markets, bringing the country’s largest stock exchange by trading activity to the listed market.
